$comment: Hand-picked resources for /resources. Check every link before adding it, describe it in our own words, and pair it with a lesson slug from content/learn when one fits.

resources.title: Elements of AI
resources.description: A friendly online course from the University of Helsinki and MinnaLearn on what AI can and can't do, with no maths or programming needed.

resources.title: Intro to Large Language Models
resources.description: Andrej Karpathy's one-hour talk on what an LLM is, how it's trained and where it's heading. The best single video to watch before or after meeting the LLM.

resources.title: Tiktokenizer
resources.description: Paste any text and watch it split into tokens and token IDs, right in the browser. The quickest way to try what the tokens lesson describes.

resources.title: But what is a neural network? (3Blue1Brown)
resources.description: Grant Sanderson's animated series on how neural networks see and learn, with pictures doing most of the work. Start with chapter 1 and carry on from there.

resources.title: Google Colab
resources.description: Run Python notebooks in the browser, with some free GPU time. Use it for any code in our lessons without installing anything on your laptop.

resources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
resources.description: Google's hands-on introduction to machine learning, with videos, visualisations and coding exercises. Good once you're comfortable with a little Python.

resources.title: Generative AI for Beginners
resources.description: Microsoft's open course for developers who want to build with LLMs: prompts, chat apps, search apps and more, each lesson with code you can run.

resources.title: Large Language Models with Semantic Search
resources.description: A short DeepLearning.AI course with Cohere on embeddings, dense retrieval and reranking, with Python notebooks. It builds directly on the embeddings lesson.

resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
resources.description: Learn to use, fine-tune and share transformer models with the Hugging Face libraries. A practical next step after the Transformer lesson.

resources.title: Ollama
resources.description: Download and run open models such as Llama, Gemma and Mistral on your own computer with one command, and call them from your code.

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need
resources.description: The 2017 paper that introduced the Transformer, the design behind today's LLMs. Read the introduction and look at the figures first.

resources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
resources.description: The paper that named retrieval-augmented generation. Read it after the RAG lesson to see where the idea came from.

resources.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
resources.description: Showed that asking a model to write out its steps improves its answers on maths and logic problems. A key paper behind today's reasoning models.

resources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
resources.description: An interactive book that teaches deep learning with the maths, the explanation and runnable code side by side.

resources.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
resources.description: Andrej Karpathy builds neural networks and a small GPT from an empty file, line by line, in Python. Best saved for after the capstone lesson.

resources.title: Deep Learning
resources.description: The classic textbook by Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, covering the maths and theory of neural networks in depth.
